The CPU base does both: src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:295-298 sets slab_volfactor = auto_slab_volfactor(...) before the order loop, and :354-366 re-derives it after adjust_gewald() and iterates (up to 5 times, erroring out if it does not converge), then prints 'auto slab volfactor' (:394-397). src/kspace.cpp:523-530 accepts 'kspace_modify slab auto' for any style with pppmflag set (PPPMKokkos inherits pppmflag=1 from PPPM) and leaves slab_volfactor = 1.0 for init() to fix; nothing in PPPMKokkos::init rejects it. With slab_volfactor stuck at 1.0, zprd_slab == zprd, gc->set_zfactor(1.0) inserts no vacuum, and slabcorr() still applies the EW3DC dipole correction because slabflag == 1 -- wrong energies/z-forces with no warning (kspace_modify's own log line at src/kspace.cpp:679 still says 'Slab volfactor is determined automatically').

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING. (1) The cited counter-example is wrong: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_kokkos.cpp:76-85 has the identical unguarded destroy/create, and so do ~187 files under src/KOKKOS (grep 'destroy_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom);'); the guarded 'if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom)' form exists only in a newer subset (bond/angle/dihedral/improper styles). So this is the dominant package idiom, not a divergence, and the CPU base is not a valid comparison either since PPPMKokkos calls ev_init(eflag,vflag,0) (alloc=0), i.e. the base deliberately does not manage these arrays. (2) The unconditional re-create is load-bearing for correctness: Kokkos value-initializes a freshly created View, and with alloc=0 nothing else zeroes eatom/vatom before the accumulation kernels, so a naive guard would leave stale per-atom energies from the previous step.
fix: Optional performance cleanup only: 'if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"pppm:eatom"); d_eatom = k_eatom.view<DeviceType>(); } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);' and the same for k_vatom. The deep_copy is mandatory, not optional -- without it the reused view keeps the previous step's values.
